old: Roman soldiers' pay was once connected, in a roundabout way, to an everyday seasoning.
That seasoning was salt — this word's Latin ancestor was built directly from the Latin word for it.
The same Latin word for salt also gives English salad, sauce, and sausage — and lives on in the phrase “worth one's salt.”
clues: This everyday workplace noun began as an allowance for Roman soldiers, traditionally linked to salt, a commodity so valuable it may once have been part of what they received.
It is the fixed yearly sum an employer pays you, divided into regular paychecks, unlike an hourly wage that rises and falls with the hours you work.
Job ads promise a competitive one, and its salty Latin root also gives English salad, sauce, sausage, and the phrase "worth one's salt."
